title: The Books Trapped in the Return Chute
central_conflict: the library return chute accepted books but none reached the collection basket
decisive_choice: a spring-loaded safety flap had been reattached backward after cleaning
resolution: closed the chute for repairs and restored the flap orientation before testing returns
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, fox and rabbit discovered the library return chute accepted books but none reached the collection basket before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Fox attempted an immediate fix, but they widened the outer opening but the books still piled up inside; rabbit stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Rabbit examined the evidence and realized a spring-loaded safety flap had been reattached backward after cleaning; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.

With the visiting readers watching, they closed the chute for repairs and restored the flap orientation before testing returns, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

title: The Robot That Watered Only Half the Beds
central_conflict: the garden robot drove every planned row but left one side of each bed dry
decisive_choice: the spray nozzle pointed inward whenever the robot arm pivoted around a corner
resolution: repositioned the nozzle and checked even water coverage with measuring cups
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, fox and rabbit discovered the garden robot drove every planned row but left one side of each bed dry before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.

Rabbit examined the evidence and realized the spray nozzle pointed inward whenever the robot arm pivoted around a corner; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.

title: The Ribbons That Clung to the Roof
central_conflict: the parade ribbons stuck to the plastic canopy instead of fluttering overhead
decisive_choice: rubbing against the dry plastic canopy had built up static electricity
resolution: replaced the rubbing contact with a grounded mounting strip and tested the ribbons
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, fox and rabbit discovered the parade ribbons stuck to the plastic canopy instead of fluttering overhead before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Fox attempted an immediate fix, but they cut longer ribbons but each new strand clung to the same surface; rabbit stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Rabbit examined the evidence and realized rubbing against the dry plastic canopy had built up static electricity; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.

With the visiting readers watching, they replaced the rubbing contact with a grounded mounting strip and tested the ribbons, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.
